text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.
LONDON - Stocks in London fell as sluggishness on Wall Street and an unwinding of options pressured the market. The FTSE 100 ended 19.3 points lower at 4,336.8, for a drop of 4.2 points for the week.

FRANKFURT - German shares edged lower, with sentiment muted by a lower, stable dollar and overnight weakness on Wall Street. The DAX-30 index fell 11.94 points to 3,184.09, for a loss of 64.09 since last week.
PARIS - French stocks lost ground, with the blue-chip CAC-40 index off 12.40 points to 2,562.84, for a loss of 64.58 on the week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended slightly lower in a consolidation of recent gains while market interest focused on UBS and on the expiry of options and futures. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 3.95 points to 2,871.24, for a gain of 31.75 on the week.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended little changed after the market benchmark wandered in a narrow range for most of the day. The Nikkei 225 fell 17.17 points to 19,034.54. For the week it rose 312.54.

HONG KONG - Calm was restored to the Hong Kong stock market after Thursday's dramatic surge and shares overcame profit-taking pressures to finish higher. The Hang Seng Index rose 33.52 points to 13,444.85, capping a rise of 331.59 from a week ago.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks ended barely changed after early Wall Street-induced selling in the banks slowed and support for mining companies emerged. The All Ordinaries index fell 1 point to 2,475.3, capping a drop of 7.3 on the week.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold stocks jumped as bullion prices rebounded while industrial issues drifted. The gold index rose 46.9 points to 1,517.8, capping a gain of 122.7 from last Friday; the overall index rose 21.5 points to 7,124.1, a gain of 103.4 for the week; the industrial index shed 12.4 points to 8,379.3. It rose 74 for the week.
